title: Customer threads: impact matrix & micro-proposals (Oct 2027)
content:
Executive summary:

This note consolidates ~45 customer threads (Q3–Q4 2027) into a compact impact matrix and 7 small, testable micro-proposals. Goal: move from broad asks to scoped experiments we can ship in 1–6 weeks. This is intentionally lightweight — many threads are partial/inconsistent. Use this as a launchpad for product + engineering quick wins and hypothesis-driven validation.

What data went in: 
- CS intake form exports (July–Oct 2027) filtered for 'inference' and 'cost' categories
- 12 recorded customer calls (CS call logs) + 18 Slack escalations
- Replicated 8 reproducible repro steps in the sandbox where possible

Topline signals (clustered):
1) Predictable tail latency pain: intermittent 95/99 spikes when multi-tenant hosted falls back to alternative model variants (12 customers; enterprise and midmarket).
2) Cost-variability surprise: token billing compounding across retries + streaming interactions (9 customers; ML platform teams).
3) Observability gaps: missing per-route token breakdown and token attribution across chained calls (15 customers).
4) Private infra onboarding friction: VPN/KMS misconfiguration causes long onboarding cycles (6 customers).
5) Model downgrade fidelity concern: automatic fallback emits style shifts / hallucination regressions (8 customers).

Representative customer quotes (sanitized):
- "We saw 2–3x cost in one week after a spike — no idea why." — midmarket search product
- "When the model falls back it sounds… different. Users notice and conversion drops." — ecommerce personalization
- "We need a single view of token cost per API route; right now we stitch logs in different systems." — platform team

Impact-effort matrix (summary rows):
- High impact, low effort: per-route token breakdown in console (Impact: H, Effort: L) -> Quick win (1–2 weeks)
- High impact, medium effort: bounded fallback policy with probe + labeling (Impact: H, Effort: M) -> 3–6 weeks
- High impact, high effort: private onboarding automation (templates + infra operator) (Impact: H, Effort: H) -> >6 weeks
- Medium impact, low effort: billing alert templates for unusual weekly spike patterns (Impact: M, Effort: L) -> 1 week
- Medium impact, medium effort: streaming retry accounting change (Impact: M, Effort: M) -> 3 weeks

Micro-proposals (scoped experiments):
1) Per-route token dashboard (console + daily CSV export)
   - Scope: show tokens consumed by route, model variant, and time window (last 24h / 7d)
   - Why: removes stitch-work for customers and immediately reduces support churn
   - Success metric: reduce churn tickets asking "why cost increased" by 40% in 30 days (tracked via CS-queue)
   - Owner: Product (Console), Eng (Observability)

2) Fallback fidelity probe: soft-probe + early labeling
   - Scope: when fallback to variant B occurs, send a small, non-billing probe to evaluate output divergence for the same prompt and emit a fidelity score in traces
   - Why: surface regressions and allow canary rollback logic or informed SLA caveats
   - Success metric: surface 90% of perceived fidelity regressions before CS escalations
   - Owner: Serving runtime + Applied ML

3) Billing spike detector + templated response playbook
   - Scope: heuristic detector that flags >x% weekly token increase per org and auto-populates an incident template for CS
   - Why: quick mitigation for surprise costs; reduce repeated manual triage
   - Success metric: mean time to first response from CS < 6 hours for flagged spikes
   - Owner: Customer Success + Billing analytics

4) Streaming retry accounting fix (prototype)
   - Scope: ensure retries do not double-count tokens in the billing exporter for streaming endpoints; provide opt-in behavior initially
   - Why: customers report billing > perceived usage during intermittent network glitches
   - Success metric: reproduce previous overbilling case and confirm corrected export
   - Owner: Infra + Billing

5) Private deployment onboarding checklist + infra templates
   - Scope: curated Terraform + KMS playbooks for top-3 customer environments + packet capture troubleshooting template
   - Why: reduces ramp time and SRE burden for regulated customers
   - Success metric: reduce mean onboarding time from 28d -> 14d for pilot customers
   - Owner: Private Deployments + Solutions Eng

6) Per-request token attribution SDK helper (client-side)
   - Scope: small open-source helper that annotates chained calls and emits a single request-id to Redwood for attribution
   - Why: simplifies customer instrumentation and improves accuracy of per-route dashboards
   - Success metric: adoption by 5 pilot customers in 60 days; fewer attribution tickets
   - Owner: Developer Experience (SDKs)

7) Canary rollback playbook with automatic fallbacks to baseline model variant
   - Scope: rollout policy change — when quality probe score degrades >t for canary, automatically route to baseline for that org for n minutes while alerting CS
   - Why: preserve UX while mitigating silent degradations
   - Success metric: zero major UX regressions in pilot canary rollouts (2 customers)
   - Owner: Platform + Product

Open questions and risks: 
- Privacy: the soft-probe (micro-proposal #2) must be optional and consented to in enterprise agreements; check legal and data retention constraints (linked: REDW-4023).
- Billing attribution complexity: retrofitting accurate attribution for chained streaming calls could require schema changes to the billing export. Is opt-in acceptable?
- Sizing: some customers request full per-token lineage (very high effort) — we should steer toward pragmatic SDK + dashboard approach first.

Quick wins suggested for next 2 sprints: 
- Ship per-route token dashboard MVP (micro-proposal #1) as internal beta to top 10 customers (2-week effort)
- Implement billing spike detector template and CS playbook (1 week)
- Triage two highest-severity billing bugs (CS-8821, REDW-4023) with debug runbooks and root cause notes

Operational notes / process: 
- Triage owner: Miguel Santos will own the spike detector build; Leah Kim will coordinate pilot of the token dashboard with 5 customers (contact list appended).
- PRs and tracking: open epic CS-THREADS-2027 in Jira; link individual tickets for each micro-proposal (owners to create by 2027-10-25).

Appendix: contact list (pilot customers)
- Acme Personalization — primary: jordan@acme.com, engineering lead: Priya R (SLACK: @priya_acme)
- NovaSearch — primary: kevin@novasearch.com
- Shopwell — primary: denise@shopwell.io

Appendix: raw snippets from threads (sanitized):
- "We got billed for 400k tokens for a session that our dashboard shows as 90k -> something double counted." (NovaSearch)
- "Can you give us a way to pin models per route and guarantee no automatic fallback for our org?" (Enterprise finance request)

Next steps (owners and dates):
- 2027-10-25: Owners to create Jira epic + tickets (ALL OWNERS)
- 2027-11-05: Console: token dashboard MVP internal beta (Leah Kim)
- 2027-11-10: Billing: spike detector in production with CS playbook (Miguel Santos)
- 2027-11-20: Runtime: begin prototype for fallback fidelity probe (Tom Berger + Applied ML)

Notes to self / loose thoughts: 
- Consider adding a low-friction "billing dispute" button in console tied to CS workflow — might cut time-to-resolution by 50%.
- Use feature flags for any automatic routing/fallback changes; surface explicit "why switched" message to end-users where possible.

If you want a trimmed CSV of the 45 threads (id, customer, signal cluster, severity, suggested micro-proposal) I can export it — specify fields and I'll drop into the JIRA epic.

Prepared by: Aisha Patel (Customer Success)
